rules.title: .NET 9 reaches end of support on 2026-11-10
rules.summary: .NET 9 (Standard Term Support) is scheduled to reach the end of its support on 2026-11-10, according to Microsoft's releases index. After that date Microsoft no longer ships security or quality fixes for it. The same line applies to the SDK that carries it, so a global.json pinning an SDK 9.0.x is reported too.

sources.title: .NET releases index (channel, support phase, end-of-life date)

constraints: Move the project files, global.json, CI images, and container base images to the same release line; a mix hides the old runtime.
Read the breaking-changes list of each release between the old and new line before raising the target.
This line is still supported today; the rule is a warning ahead of the announced date, so plan the move before it.

steps.title: Raise the target framework
steps.instructions: Change the reported TargetFramework (or TargetFrameworks entry) from the 9.0 line to a line that will still be supported after 2026-11-10, for example net10.0.

steps.title: Raise the SDK pin
steps.instructions: Update the sdk version in global.json to an SDK of the same supported line, or remove the pin if the repository does not need one.

steps.title: Align CI and container images
steps.instructions: Update setup-dotnet versions in CI and the mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet images in Dockerfiles to the new line.

verification.purpose: Confirm the SDK and runtime in use are the intended supported release.
Build and test every project on the new target.

rules.title: WindowsAzure.Storage is deprecated on NuGet
rules.summary: Microsoft marked every version of WindowsAzure.Storage as deprecated (reason: Legacy) because the package has been obsolete since 2023-03-31 and is no longer maintained or monitored. The deprecation names Azure.Storage.Common as the replacement.
rules.replacement: Azure.Storage.Blobs, Azure.Storage.Queues, Azure.Storage.Files.Shares, or Azure.Data.Tables, with Azure.Storage.Common

constraints: Keep the data format and the blob, queue, and table names the same; only the client library changes.

steps.title: Move to the Azure.Storage.* packages
steps.instructions: Replace WindowsAzure.Storage with the package for each service in use (Azure.Storage.Blobs, Azure.Storage.Queues, Azure.Storage.Files.Shares, or Azure.Data.Tables) and update CloudStorageAccount and CloudBlobClient code to the new client types.

verification.purpose: Build and test after the client library change.

rules.title: Microsoft.Azure.DocumentDB is deprecated on NuGet
rules.summary: NuGet marks all 36 listed versions of Microsoft.Azure.DocumentDB as deprecated (reason: Legacy). The publisher's message: "Please note, this package is obsolete as of 3/31/2023 and is no longer maintained or monitored. Microsoft encourages you to upgrade to the replacement package, Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos, to continue receiving updates. Refer to our deprecation policy (https://aka.ms/azsdk/support-policies) for more details."

constraints: Keep the account, database, and container names and the stored documents the same; only the client library changes.
The Cosmos DB v3 SDK names collections "containers" and replaces DocumentClient with CosmosClient; check queries and partition key handling after the move.

steps.title: Move to Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos
steps.instructions: Replace Microsoft.Azure.DocumentDB with Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos and update DocumentClient code to CosmosClient, Database, and Container.

verification.purpose: Build and test after the client library change.

rules.title: Microsoft.Azure.ServiceBus is deprecated on NuGet
rules.summary: NuGet marks all 33 listed versions of Microsoft.Azure.ServiceBus as deprecated (reason: Legacy). The publisher's message: "Please note, this package is obsolete as of 9/30/2026 and is no longer maintained or monitored. Microsoft encourages you to upgrade to the replacement package, Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus, to continue receiving updates. Refer to the migration guide (https://aka.ms/azsdk/net/migrate/sb) for guidance on upgrading. Refer to our deprecation policy (https://aka.ms/azsdk/support-policies) for more details."

constraints: Keep the namespace, queue, topic, and subscription names the same; only the client library changes.
Read the migration guide first: message settlement, sessions, and retry options moved to ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusSender, ServiceBusReceiver, and ServiceBusProcessor.

steps.title: Move to Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus
steps.instructions: Replace Microsoft.Azure.ServiceBus with Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus and update QueueClient, TopicClient, and SubscriptionClient code to ServiceBusClient with senders, receivers, or processors.

verification.purpose: Build and test after the client library change.

rules.title: Microsoft.Azure.Storage.Blob is deprecated on NuGet
rules.summary: NuGet marks all 24 listed versions of Microsoft.Azure.Storage.Blob as deprecated (reason: Legacy). The publisher's message: "Please note, this package is obsolete as of 3/31/2023 and is no longer maintained or monitored. Microsoft encourages you to upgrade to the replacement package, Azure.Storage.Blobs, to continue receiving updates. Refer to the migration guide (https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/master/sdk/storage/Azure.Storage.Blobs/AzureStorageNetMigrationV12.md) for guidance on upgrading. Refer to our deprecation policy (https://aka.ms/azsdk/support-policies) for more details."

constraints: Keep the container and blob names and the stored data the same; only the client library changes.
Read the v12 migration guide: CloudStorageAccount and CloudBlobClient become BlobServiceClient, and blob handles become BlobClient types.

steps.title: Move to Azure.Storage.Blobs
steps.instructions: Replace Microsoft.Azure.Storage.Blob with Azure.Storage.Blobs and update CloudStorageAccount, CloudBlobClient, CloudBlobContainer, and CloudBlockBlob code to BlobServiceClient, BlobContainerClient, and BlobClient.

verification.purpose: Build and test after the client library change.
